newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey, Israel see jump in trade after trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Turkey, Israel see jump in trade after trade deal.

text.p: A recent free trade accord between Turkey and Israel will more than double the bilateral trade volume this year and next, a senior Turkish trade official said on Monday.

"Now that the agreement is in effect, we expect the trade volume to rise to $1 billion this year and to $2 billion next year," said Reyhan Atmaca, head of the European Union (EU) department at the government's foreign trade undersecretariat.
"The agreement, which has a transition period until the year 2000, will open new markets for Turkey and Israel," she told a meeting of Turkish and Israeli businessmen in the town of Izmir.

Turkey and Israel, which had a bilateral trade volume of $460 million in 1996, signed the agreement in March 1996. But the deal waited in parliament during the office of the former Islamist-led government until it took effect in May.
Atmaca said the free trade agreement would allow Turkey and Israel to enter into markets that were otherwise difficult to trade in.
"Turkey will be a bridge for Israel to sell its goods to (former Soviet) Turkic republics in Central Asia, and Turkey can do more trade with the United States and Canada via Israel," she said.
"This covers some 85 percent of our goods and 90 percent of Israel's goods that can move freely in new markets. That will boost the competitive edge of the two countries," she said.
Some 40 Israeli businessmen representing agricultural, textile, cosmetics, health and food sectors began a four-day visit to Turkey on Monday to meet Turkish businessmen in Izmir and Istanbul.
